common_assertions: Every authority/edit is produced by an ordinary public writer or import of independently verified exact signed public bytes. Never insert, rewrite or copy a valid private edit row, key, store, signature or admission with SQL.

The original SSH key remains only in the original owner's signer HOME. No daemon original-key file, person agent or inherited SSH_AUTH_SOCK is present in the new-reader fixtures. Explicit matching original signing occurs through its typed CLI/action path on that same machine.

A real same-predecessor fork is retained as both maximal policy heads. No legacy version/hash winner or SQL displacement is used. The explicit resolver names every known head in predecessors and resolves, uses retained maximum+1, and preserves one exact admitted branch's entire content and edits apart from version and times.

Hash every frozen start/signed POLICY_REFERENCE and its original proof-container bytes before and after recovery. Preserve signed_version, signed_at and retained dropped strings. Document permitted state/timestamp transitions separately.
Read snapshots are coherent SQLite read transactions or stopped snapshots. Record named row differences and hash-only private-file custody. No immutable/nolock live DB copy or private DB export.
Authority decisions use an explicitly opted-in monotonic DEC clock. Transport, cache, waits and deadlines remain real. No rewind, expired-window extension, replacement key or fabricated consent.

First failure stops its dependent path and preserves the actual stopped fixture, exact public request/response bytes, pre/post public clock/hash observations, protected private hash manifest, artifact SHA and source. Passed functions are not replayed in a narrow continuation.

cases.name: actual_sibling_deny_requires_all_head_resolution_and_blocks_new_edit_signing
cases.fixture: Two actual current same-person hosts A and B. A signs a reviewer-access withdrawal while B independently signs an unrelated addition from the identical baseline. A reserves a newer sequence while the withdrawal is still settled; both signed siblings are then imported. A has no automatic original signer.
steps: Use actual top-level allow network --agent reviewer --no-tasks for the necessary baseline, checking exact documented message-only settings. Prove a fresh actual B-to-A reviewer message is accepted under that exact current policy. Retain its request ID/receipt; use a fresh ID for each later authorization check.

Apply actual top-level deny network --agent reviewer on A and retain its exact start/signed references. Reserve one newer A sequence while the deny is settled; do not sign it. B creates its sibling through the advanced access allow frontend from the unchanged baseline using its actual current policy device.

Import both complete signed policies through the current member catalog route. Verify both heads remain, current policy is unusable, reapply-preview and new reservations refuse the fork, and unsigned reservations stay unsigned.

Explicitly review and apply one ordinary resolver selecting the exact admitted B branch with all known predecessors/resolves and maximum+1, current independent A original authority and exact complete proof closure.

Build otherwise valid NEW-sequence ordinary action and policy-claim candidates against the resulting unique head, each carrying the still-newest reserved A sequence. Attempt approved preparation/signing, without first reapplying the old deny.
assert: The resolver consumes no reservation, local edit counter or policy_claim and never fabricates a signed reference for the unsigned row. Its full content and entire edits match B's branch except the permitted generation/time fields.

The omitted actual signed A deny remains unsettled under the unique resolved head. NEW reservation and both NEW-sequence action/claim signature paths return state_conflict before any signature, policy admission, maximum advance, settlement, capability or delivery mutation; only the named monotonic guard exception is allowed on refusal.

Although the selected B branch contains the reviewer permission, a fresh authenticated B message to that actual reviewer is forbidden and creates no accepted message. This proves immediate retained withdrawal enforcement, not model/session execution.
All original references/proof bytes and never-signed reservation fields remain exact. A closed older row, if independently present, remains closed.

cases.name: actual_sibling_untrust_remains_enforced_before_external_original_native_recovery
cases.fixture: Separate actual same-person two-host fixture. An actual A fixture MCP source is opened to B, with no policy share or manual-grant fallback. The baseline trusts B. A removes B through native untrust, while B independently signs an unrelated sibling addition. Use the same legitimate fork/resolver construction as the deny case, without invoking that case function.
steps: Prove B sees the exact source through self and a harmless fixture operation is accepted before untrust. Retain the source settings/snapshot and exact current binding/host evidence.
Apply actual A untrust, reserve a newer unsigned local sequence, retain both real sibling heads, and explicitly resolve all heads to B's exact branch, which still trusts B.
Attempt a new reservation and an otherwise valid already-reserved NEW-sequence candidate before reapplication. Query listing and submit a fresh exact self-cited fixture operation from actual B.
assert: The actual A untrust remains a live signed unsettled obligation; neither larger sequence nor explicit branch resolution settles or overwrites its frozen references.

New-edit/signature guards refuse with state_conflict and no signature/admission/settlement. The actual source is absent from B's authorized listing and its otherwise valid fresh self-cited call is forbidden. No accepted call or source invocation occurs.

Current A/B memberships, bindings, selected B seed/provider, source open-list and source snapshot remain unchanged; denial is attributable to retained untrust rather than a broken fixture source or expired authority.

cases.name: pure_reapply_preview_then_external_native_recovery_precedes_unrelated_new_edit
cases.fixture: Continue each actual unique-head deny/untrust fixture above. Preserve its old unsigned reservation and all signed frozen history. The original is unavailable to the daemon and exists only on A's CLI signer HOME.
steps: Read summary/current policy/provider and take coherent all-row/private-file hash snapshots. Call exact reapply-preview with the explicit matching original key, then repeat after a real second or later monotonic decision time. Also exercise the no-unsettled read after actual recovery.

Check the exact six-field preview, canonical payload Base64 and decoded typed policy, current root/predecessor, retained maximum+1, actual highest unsettled old sequence and other hosts' exact edits. Do not demand equal issued times across independent previews.

Invoke a new unrelated top-level allow network --agent fresh-native --no-tasks with the external original key. Retain typed-slot and admitted catalog observations showing an actual old-sequence reapply first, then a reloaded baseline and a separately reserved new mutation. The separately bound timing executable also exercises actual advanced access renew.
Reopen the same store and perform fresh authenticated reviewer/self operations. Inspect exact original frozen references, dropped history and the separately abandoned unsigned reservation.
assert: Every preview, including empty and refusal paths, changes no DB row, guard, provider, event, outbox, selection, key or peer request. No-unsettled returns payload_base64 '-' and an empty sorted sequence list. Root cannot substitute for the policy owner.
The preview uses a real current scope1 path and its finite ceiling, not an unrelated broader admin8 summary deadline. The matching external original needs no daemon key import or agent.

The CLI signs only the exact reviewed ordinary payload/slots. Actual reapplication admission precedes the new reservation/new signature; native code reloads that admitted result before composing its unrelated edit. No old withdrawal is absorbed by a larger own sequence.

The final admitted policy retains the deny/untrust, and fresh actual peer requests stay denied. The old signed row's start/signed/version/signed_at/dropped bytes remain original; its permitted live state may settle or close under the contract. The unsigned reservation is never invented as signed.
No private original, host seed or device seed crosses a machine boundary. This is foreground native policy recovery, not separate-machine custody or installed acceptance.

cases.name: colliding_display_marker_groups_converge_in_same_pass_without_removing_independent_baseline_permission
cases.fixture: Separate actual fixture per variant. Baseline has two same-agent rules R1/R2 with distinct full settings and principal Q. One actual local edit adds P to BOTH. The sibling's actual policy removes R1, leaves R2 without P, and independently includes a third same-agent settings key R3 with P. No SQL edit construction.
steps: Apply the exact A edit through an actual reservation and typed ordinary action. Independently sign the exact sibling policy, retain the real fork, and use the narrow explicit all-head resolver to choose that sibling content/edits.

Read the first exact reapply candidate before any reapplication signature. Complete the actual external-original reapplication, reopen and read it again. Later cause another legitimate displacement and reapply that same retained live row if it remains live; never resurrect a closed row.
Reverse the order of R1/R2 in a separately constructed actual variant. Compare semantic results and exact generated dropped group, while retaining each variant's original signed bytes.
assert: Distinct full RuleKeys remain distinct. A marker generated when R1 conflicts suppresses BOTH represented LOCAL additions of P in R1/R2 in this very first candidate, even if R2 was provisionally merged before the conflict was noticed.
The independent current-baseline R3/P permission survives. Group membership comes only from this exact frozen local delta; a similarly spelled addition in another edit is not suppressed.

The signed/admitted result equals the final converged candidate; no provisional permissive body is signed/published. Exact canonical dropped strings are sorted unique, bounded and readable on reopen. Later reapplication cannot restore the suppressed additions.
Reversing rule order produces the same authority/content outcome. Dropped status reports the conservative group loss. No full rule identity is silently collapsed to the display string.

cases.name: legitimately_written_of_markers_survive_same_store_upgrade_and_closed_rows_do_not_resurrect
cases.constructor_status: HELD pending a separate explicit historical-writer constructor offer after the new common source freeze. Prior Rust7c may be offered ONLY for this constructor; its withdrawn final-gate scope is not revived.
cases.fixture: Fresh actual A/B identities and stores. Old A actually creates its frozen edit; current B is upgraded in place and explicitly resolves a legitimate all-head fork. Import of the exact resolver into old A must actually cause its ordinary writer to retain an 'of' marker. Stop A and reopen that SAME actual store with the newly offered reader. Original A key stays on A; no private row/store/key copy or rewrite.
steps: Use actual public writers to obtain the marker. For the live variant include a real retained withdrawal that changes reapply content. For the closed variant use a real no-content-change merge that closes the row without fabricated signed history. Retain the first response even if an old reader refuses after the actual drop transaction.

Before upgrade verify the exact nonempty stored marker and its original complete start/signed containers; hash all private files and named public/edit rows. If this precondition was not actually produced, stop with constructor unevaluated.

Upgrade A in place to each separately offered new reader. Read/reopen without mutation, then apply a legitimate current reapplication on a live row. For the independently closed row retain it through another actual fork and exact all-head resolution.
assert: Only an exact alternate generated from actual frozen additions is accepted. Stored 'of' strings and original references/rows remain byte-exact on reads, no global label substring rewrite occurs, and no canonical 'in' duplicate is appended by a later write.

Actual retained alternate groups skip the same additions as canonical groups, including same-pass collision convergence and independent S protection. A valid nonempty closed row remains readable after upgrade.
The closed row remains closed across later fork/resolver reconciliation and contributes no reapplication. No old retired intent is resurrected.
A failed old constructor or missing legitimate alias provenance is not a compatibility PASS. Malformed private-row injection is not authorized by this case.

cases.name: delayed_private_preparation_preserves_payload_expiry_and_stale_intent_does_not_block_native_renewal
cases.fixture: Fresh current original-owner network with no unsettled edit. Daemon original signing is unavailable. Prepare a valid exact ordinary policy renewal with issued T0 at a later monotonic DEC time T1=T0+2 seconds; finite original parents outlive all observations.
steps: First prepare at T1, explicitly approve at T0+3, and capture the actual unsigned template/slot plus named private intent. Honestly generate the exact external original signature at T0+3 while valid, retain its public request unchanged, and withhold submission. Stop/reopen without changing keys/provider/consent.

At T0+301 read/retry the same approved action by its exact immutable action ID. Allow an exact ordinary200 result or structured expired diagnostic; verify the retained named private intent independently. Submit only the unchanged public signed request generated while valid, without invoking the old original signer after its window.

Use a fresh current native access renewal with the matching external original. Observe its new actual typed intent and successful admission, then inspect both old and new intent records and old source references.
assert: Actual first created_at is T1, strictly greater than payload issued_at T0; expiry is exactly T0+300, so Issued<=Created<Expires. Approval, GET, retry and signature submission never backdate or refresh these fields.

A valid interrupted stale private record remains readable and internally valid despite unequal initial times; its public action GET may return structured expired. Refusal of stale submission has no signature/admission/max/edit/provider/event mutation beyond explicitly named guard/terminal rules; no payload replacement, new late original signature or consent replay.

The later independently reviewed native renewal succeeds under current scope1 authority and a new fixed payload time. The old stale intent cannot corrupt reopen or permanently block the legitimate renewal. Its signed/public bytes and review/history are retained rather than rewritten to hide age.

cases.name: new_preparation_at_fixed_expiry_refuses_but_existing_honest_signing_age300_is_inclusive
cases.fixture: Fresh independent original-owner fixture. Two otherwise valid exact next-policy payloads have issued T0 and the same next generation, with distinct valid finite deadlines to obtain distinct operation identities. Prepare/approve only the first before expiry; do not apply either yet.
steps: Prepare and approve the first at T0+2. Retain its exact ready external-original slot and no submitted signature.
At T0+300 first submit the distinct second payload as NEW preparation, then honestly sign and submit the already prepared first payload at that same fixed decision second.
assert: The distinct new preparation refuses before persistence at equality with its fixed issued+300 expiry. It creates no intent/template/reservation/signature/admission/max/outbox/provider/event; only the named guard exception may persist. Do not infer an unspecified error precedence from multiple invalid preconditions.

The original already prepared and approved payload may honestly sign at age exactly300 inclusive under valid current finite proofs. It applies once, with exact original payload/created/approved/expiry values and no renewed local window.
This checks the new runtime distinction between first preparation and an existing honest signing slot. It does not repeat or relabel historical pure T1/T300/T301 results.
